sections.title: What is Covered by GEHA Insurance?
body: If you are a member of GEHA, you may be eligible for full or partial coverage of addiction treatment programs. GEHA can provide coverage for various treatment programs, including detoxification, inpatient rehab programs, various forms of outpatient treatment programs, medication-assisted treatment, and other forms of behavioral therapy.

GEHA does require that your addiction treatment provider is nationally certified and licensed within their state for their members to receive coverage. This is to ensure that you receive care at an evidence-based and effective treatment facility.

sections.title: Is Drug Rehab Treatment Covered by GEHA?
body: GEHA does provide coverage for its members who are in need of drug rehab. This includes inpatient and outpatient treatment services. GEHA will provide medical coverage for individuals who have already participated in and completed an addiction treatment program if it is medically necessary at this time.

Many individuals who engage in inpatient addiction treatment programs, especially detoxification programs, are exposed to medication-assisted treatment to help them cope with uncomfortable symptoms they experience. Some individuals will continue with medication-assisted treatment in early recovery to help relieve some negative symptoms, such as cravings. GEHA members are eligible for this form of treatment.

If you are a GEHA member and find yourself struggling with another mental health concern alongside an addiction, GEHA will provide coverage for mental health treatment as well. It is common for individuals struggling with an addiction to have an accompanying mental health concern. Research has shown us that individuals in this situation have a healthier recovery if they receive treatment for both concerns at the same time.

sections.title: How Long Will GEHA Cover Addiction Treatment?
body: The length of time that GEHA will provide coverage will vary for each member. GEHA makes its decision based on what is deemed medically necessary for you. Since there is no “cookie cutter” form of addiction treatment, you can expect your needs to be different from other members.

As an example, GEHA will take into consideration the severity of your abuse, the length of time you have been struggling, any medical implications from your use, additional mental health needs, and other potential risk factors before making their decision regarding the length of your coverage.
